As LLMs increasingly saturate these benchmarks\u2014with frontier models exceeding 85% on FLARE, FinQA, and related datasets\u2014the field lacks tools to distinguish genuine economic understanding from sophisticated pattern matching. We introduce EconBench, a hierarchically structured evaluation framework comprising 4,200 expert-curated items spanning five reasoning strata: definitional recall, conceptual application, multi-step causal inference, equilibrium analysis under uncertainty, and institutional-context-dependent reasoning. Items are constructed to resist memorization through (a) novel scenario framing that preserves causal structure while altering surface features, (b) deliberate inclusion of plausible distractor reasoning chains, and (c) adversarial perturbation of standard textbook formulations. We evaluate fourteen frontier and open-weight LLMs and find systematic performance stratification: all models perform competitively at Strata 1\u20132 (definitional and applied), but diverge sharply at Strata 3\u20135, with the best model (GPT-4o) achieving only 51.3% at Stratum 5 compared to an expert economist baseline of 84.7%. We further demonstrate that chain-of-thought prompting improves Strata 3\u20134 performance but produces overconfident wrong reasoning at Stratum 5, where models construct internally consistent but economically invalid arguments at a higher rate under CoT than without. We release EconBench, item construction protocols, and economist-annotated reasoning chains to support evaluation research.
